narrative_summary: SPX closed at 7,748.50, up 0.26%, reclaiming the flattening 20-day SMA and ending three straight lower closes, but still failing for a seventh session to confirm the 7,793.68 record high from August 5. The structural skeleton is intact and credit is the tightest of the year (junk spread 1.22, VIX 14.55 at a one-year low), yet the internals that would validate a breakout remain thin: net new 52-week highs at 0.97, McClellan only just back above 1,000, and money flow far below its August 4 peak at a comparable price. Valuation is restrictive with ERP at 0.28% inside the ceiling band and forward PE 20.15x, and the Monte Carlo edge — 64.21% adjusted up-first — fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for the fifteenth consecutive session. Posture stays trim-bias and patient: no adds here, monitor 7,610 as the first meaningful re-entry test.

McClellan Volume Summation Index has recovered to 1,005 from the 826 cycle low, its best reading since early June — the first breadth improvement of the arc (chart 11).

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: McClellan Volume Summation has turned up decisively to 1,005 from the 826 cycle low, the first meaningful breadth repair of the advance, and the Fear & Greed headline at 62 sits in greed with safe-haven demand favoring equities — participation may be catching up to price.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Net new 52-week highs have sagged to 0.97, the weakest of the one-year chart and far below the 6.5 February peak, while price sits within 0.6% of an all-time high. Headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership, and McClellan at ~1,005 is still barely above its own cycle-low shelf.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: 5-day MFI has recovered to ~50 from the ~22 washout of Aug 6 and daily MFI holds ~69 on the 1-month/3-month charts, with daily RSI stabilizing near 55-64 — momentum has reset without price damage, a classic consolidation signature.

Longer-timeframe divergences carry more weight.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while MFI or RSI makes a lower high. Longer timeframe divergences carry more weight than short-term ones.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Today's +0.26% close reclaimed the 20-day SMA after a single-session breach, ended three consecutive lower closes, and the 1-month chart shows the consolidation holding above the rising 50-day — a textbook bull-flag pause rather than a top.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: The 7,793.68 swing high from Aug 5 remains unconfirmed for a seventh session and the 7,700-7,794 zone is now a multi-week shelf of small-bodied doji and spinning-top candles at the upper Bollinger band — the profile of distribution, not accumulation. conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A close back above the 20-day SMA after a breakdown is a meaningful improvement in short-term structure; a single new-high session is provisional until confirmed.

primary_tension: The most benign credit and volatility backdrop of the entire arc (junk spread 1.22 at year-lows, VIX 14.55 at a one-year low, 50-day above a rising 200-day, price above every fib) is colliding with a seventh consecutive failure to confirm the 7,793.68 record high inside a widening 7,700-7,794 distribution shelf, participation that remains the weakest of the year at record price (net new 52-week highs 0.97, McClellan only just back above 1,000), a multi-session money-flow divergence (5-day MFI ~50 versus ~91 on Aug 4 at a comparable price), extension at +9.67% above the 200-day with Moderate exhaustion, an ERP compressed to 0.28% inside the valuation-ceiling band with the re-entry floor 4.2% below spot, and a Monte Carlo edge of 64.21% that fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for a fifteenth consecutive session.
